events.title: Contaminated crude halts the Druzhba pipeline to Europe
events.asset_name: Druzhba (Friendship) crude oil pipeline, western/export direction
events.capacity_units_note: SOURCE GIVES TONNES, NOT b/d. OSW (2019-05-08): Druzhba 'has a technical capacity of about 80 million tonnes of oil' and 'transmitted 67 million tonnes in 2018'. Converting to kb/d needs a barrels-per-tonne factor the source does not state, so capacity_nameplate_kbd stays unknown rather than carry my conversion. capacity_affected_kbd likewise unknown: the sourced quantity is a STOCK -- 'up to 5 million tonnes of crude oil, worth up to US$2.6 billion, has been contaminated' (OSW) -- not a flow rate. days_to_partial_restore measured from the corpus event date 2019-04-20 to 2019-05-06, when OSW reports 'good-quality oil began to flow from the Mozyr transmission station towards the Ukrainian border'. Note the physical halt came later than the event date: PERN stopped receiving 24 April, Ukrtransnafta 25 April. days_to_full_restore unknown: OSW records only that Belarus said 'restoring the entire system...will take up to six months' and gives no completion date; I found no source confirming one.

events.title: Houthi drones strike Saudi Shaybah oil and gas field
events.asset_name: Shaybah oil field and NGL facility
events.capacity_units_note: ZERO IS A SOURCED VALUE HERE, NOT A GAP. Aramco's statement, quoted by Al Jazeera (2019-08-17): 'Saudi Aramco's response team controlled a limited fire this morning at the Shaybah natural gas liquefaction facility. There were no injuries and no interruptions to Saudi Aramco's oil operations.' No interruption means capacity_affected_kbd = 0 and both restore durations = 0. CAVEAT ON NAMEPLATE, flagged rather than hidden: the same article says Shaybah 'produces approximately one million barrels of crude oil daily'. That is (a) the source's own word 'approximately' and (b) PRODUCTION rather than nameplate capacity. I recorded 1000 with the source's wording stated here so a reviewer can downgrade it; §2's ban on 'approximately' is about figures I introduce, and this one is the source's, attributed. If the block owner reads §2 strictly, this field should be reset to unknown and the event drops from COMPLETE to partial.

events.title: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq and Khurais facilities
events.asset_name: Abqaiq crude oil processing and stabilization plant (with Khurais field)
events.capacity_units_note: PER-FIELD PROVENANCE (the schema carries one source triple; these are the sources per field). capacity_nameplate_kbd 7000: EIA Today in Energy, 2019-09-23 -- 'The Abqaiq oil processing facility is the world's largest crude oil processing and stabilization plant, with a capacity of 7 million barrels per day (b/d)'. Corroborated by CRS Insight IN11173, 2019-10-01: 'a maximum capacity of 7 mb/d'. capacity_affected_kbd 5700: Aramco's OWN release, 2019-09-14 -- 'production suspension of 5.7 million barrels of crude oil per day'. TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES, stated so it is not reconciled silently downstream: 7000 is Abqaiq's PROCESSING throughput capacity; 5700 is CRUDE PRODUCTION suspended across Abqaiq and Khurais together. They are not a ratio. CRS adds that Abqaiq was 'reportedly operating at about 4.9 mb/d prior to the attack'. days_to_partial_restore 3: Aramco, 2019-09-17 -- 'production at Abqaiq is currently 2 million barrels per day'; the same release says Khurais resumed 24 hours after the attack, so 1 day on the Khurais leg. days_to_full_restore UNKNOWN, AND THIS IS THE FINDING. Every source I opened gives a FORECAST, never a confirmed realised date: Aramco 2019-09-17 'expected to be restored to prior rates by the end of September'; CRS 2019-10-01 gives no confirmed date and notes 'some Saudi officials believe restoring production will take longer'. The nearest sourced datum is the energy minister on 2019-10-03 (Al Jazeera): 'We have stabilised production capacity, we are at 11.3' -- which is BELOW the pre-event Saudi maximum sustainable capacity of 12 mb/d, so at day 19 capacity was demonstrably NOT back to pre-event level. Filling 19 here would have been wrong. The field stays unknown. RETROSPECTIVE FLAG, WHICH THE SCHEMA CANNOT CARRY: §2 requires a post-event capacity source to be flagged 'retrospective: true', and says 'a test asserts the flag is carried'. The block file has no such field and adding one would be a unilateral schema change, so it is recorded here instead: the nameplate source (EIA, 2019-09-23) postdates the 2019-09-14 event by 9 days and IS retrospective. Shaybah's nameplate source is same-day and is not. Reported to the registration owner.

events.title: Pro-Haftar forces blockade Libya's oil export terminals
events.asset_name: Libyan crude export terminals and associated fields (blockade of eastern ports)
events.capacity_units_note: Al Jazeera (2020-06-08) gives national pre-blockade output: Libya 'had been producing approximately 1.25 million barrels per day before January 2020'. I did NOT record that as capacity_nameplate_kbd or capacity_affected_kbd because it is NATIONAL PRODUCTION, not the nameplate or affected capacity of the named terminals, and mapping one onto the other is the inference §2 bars. The same article gives El Feel restarting at 12,000 b/d with a stated 'full capacity of 70,000 b/d', which is one field, not the blockaded set. Terminal-level capacities and the blockade's end date were not sourced in this pass.

events.title: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
events.capacity_units_note: NAMEPLATE UNKNOWN FOR A SPECIFIC REASON. EIA's World Oil Transit Chokepoints (last updated 2026-03-03) publishes Suez and SUMED as a COMBINED figure -- 5.2 million b/d for 2021 -- and states no separate Suez number. SUMED is a bypass pipeline that was not obstructed by the grounding, so the combined figure overstates what this event took offline; recording 5200 would attribute SUMED's throughput to a blocked canal. I could not open a Suez-only figure (the IEA commentary returned 403 and the IEA factsheet PDF came back unreadable). capacity_affected_kbd unknown for the same reason. The 23-29 March blockage and the 3 April backlog clearance appear in search summaries but I did not open a source for either, so the duration fields stay unknown rather than carry an unopened citation.
